evidence: Ter. Ad. 1.1.44 (Lewis & Short: officium suum facere, “to do one’s duty”)
terms.comment: The word of Cicero’s Dē officiīs. Officium facere, servāre is to do one’s duty, officiō dēesse to fail in it; it is also a kindness or service done for someone, and a post or office (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: it is the duty of …, it is for … to
terms.grammar: construction: est patris, est adulēscentis + infinitive
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.122: est igitur adulēscentis majōrēs nātū verērī
terms.comment: Latin often states a duty without a noun: the genitive of the person whose part it is.

phrases.latin: est igitur adulēscentis majōrēs nātū verērī
phrases.english: so it is the duty of the young to respect their elders

phrases.latin: an id dolēs, quia illī suum officium nōn colunt, quom tu tuum facis?
phrases.english: or does it hurt you that they don’t keep their obligation while you keep yours?
